newsitem.title: KENYA: International fund begins trade at Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: International fund begins trade at Nairobi bourse.

text.p: Regent Undervalued Assets Africa, incorporated in the Cayman Islands, became the first international fund to be listed on the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) on Thursday.

The fund will be listed simultaneously at the Dublin and Botswana stock exchanges and seeks to obtain capital growth by investing in a range of undervalued opportunities in Africa, senior company officials said.

"Kenya cannot continue to play second fiddle to the developed world," said Regent's local director Julius Gecau. "Because we have no gold or oil we must use whatever opportunities we find in the world's markets."

Gecau added that Regent's listing on the Nairobi bourse was an opportunity for local investors to share in returns available in other African markets and of companies operating in Africa but listed on stock exchanges elsewhere.

Regent has been given resident status and does not have to worry about restrictive rules that affect foreign investors. The minimum investible lot is 2,500 shares held in dollars but will trade in local currency at the bourse.

The bourse began the year on a bullish streak but is currently in a lull under the weight of wary investors disappointed by year-end results released by leading banks Barclays and Standard Chartered last week.

Investment analysts said the main group of disappointed investors consisted of speculators who bought shares in anticipation of an accompanying bonus issue. They added that the lull should effectively weed out speculators, paving the way for long term investors interested in growth.
Regent is a long term investment that targets mainly Kenya's pension funds and institutional investors and will be listed on the Financials & Investments board.
